entries.title: Server Method fails to compile after upgrade to Aras Innovator 39
entries.summary: C# server Methods that used HttpContext.Current stopped compiling after moving to Aras Innovator 39 on .NET 10. Replace web-context access with Method arguments and the IOM API.
entries.content:
## Symptom

After the upgrade, saving or running several custom server Methods fails with a compile error:

```text
error CS0234: The type or namespace name 'HttpContext' does not exist in the namespace 'System.Web'
```

Affected Methods were all older utilities that read request headers or the client IP address, or built file paths with `HttpContext.Current.Server.MapPath(...)`.

## Root cause

Aras Innovator 39 runs on .NET 10 (Kestrel behind IIS). The classic ASP.NET `System.Web.HttpContext` does not exist there, so any Method that reached into the web request no longer compiles. `System.Web.HttpUtility` still exists, which is why only some Methods broke.

## Fix

1. Find every affected Method before the upgrade window:

   ```sql
   SELECT name FROM innovator.[METHOD]
   WHERE method_code LIKE '%HttpContext%' OR method_code LIKE '%MapPath%';
   ```

2. Stop reading values from the web request. Pass them in as Method arguments from the caller instead:

   ```csharp
   // Before
   string source = HttpContext.Current.Request.Headers["X-Source-System"];

   // After: the caller sends <source_system> in the Method body
   string source = this.getProperty("source_system", "unknown");
   ```

3. Replace `MapPath` with a configured base folder and `Path.Combine`. Don't hard-code backslashes, because Methods may run on Linux.

## Notes

- Run the SQL above against a copy of production early. It turns an upgrade-night surprise into a planned task.
- Recompile all Methods after the upgrade (open and save, or run a scripted AML `edit`) so errors show up before users find them.
entries.author: Maya Jansen

entries.title: IIS app pool recycling every 29 hours kills long-running Aras jobs
entries.summary: Users were logged out and a nightly import aborted at unpredictable times. The IIS default recycle interval (1740 minutes) drifts through the day; schedule the recycle at a fixed quiet time instead.
entries.content:
## Symptom

- Users occasionally lose their session in the middle of the working day.
- A long-running scheduled import stops without any error in the Aras logs.
- The problem moves: Monday at 10:00, Tuesday at 15:00, Wednesday at 20:00.

## Root cause

A new IIS app pool recycles after **1740 minutes (29 hours)** by default, so the recycle time shifts by five hours every day. Every recycle ends in-flight requests and in-memory state. The pool also shuts down after the default **20-minute idle timeout**, so the first user of the morning waits for a cold start.

Check the System event log for WAS event **5074** ("a worker process ... has requested a recycle") to confirm this.

## Fix

Recycle at a fixed time outside office hours and keep the pool warm:

```powershell
Import-Module WebAdministration
$pool = "IIS:\AppPools\InnovatorServer"

# Disable the rolling 29-hour interval
Set-ItemProperty $pool -Name recycling.periodicRestart.time -Value "00:00:00"

# Recycle once a day at 03:00 instead
Clear-ItemProperty $pool -Name recycling.periodicRestart.schedule
Set-ItemProperty $pool -Name recycling.periodicRestart.schedule -Value @{ value = "03:00:00" }

# Never shut down on idle
Set-ItemProperty $pool -Name processModel.idleTimeout -Value "00:00:00"

# Log every recycle reason to the event log
Set-ItemProperty $pool -Name recycling.logEventOnRecycle -Value "Time,Requests,Schedule,Memory,IsapiUnhealthy,OnDemand,ConfigChange,PrivateMemory"
```

## Notes

- Apply the same settings to the Vault and OAuth pools, not just the main server pool.
- Move scheduled jobs so they don't overlap the recycle window.
entries.author: Tom de Vries

entries.title: SQL Server collation conflict after restoring the Aras database on a new server
entries.summary: Queries using temp tables failed with "Cannot resolve the collation conflict" after moving the database to a new SQL Server instance with a different server collation.
entries.content:
## Symptom

After restoring the production backup on a new SQL Server instance, some reports and custom stored procedures failed:

```text
Msg 468, Level 16, State 9
Cannot resolve the collation conflict between "SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS"
and "Latin1_General_CI_AS" in the equal to operation.
```

Standard Aras functionality worked. Only custom SQL that used `#temp` tables failed.

## Root cause

A restored database keeps its own collation, but temp tables live in `tempdb`, which uses the **server** collation. The new instance was installed with a different default, so every join between a temp table and a real table compared two different collations.

```sql
SELECT SERVERPROPERTY('Collation')                          AS server_collation,
       DATABASEPROPERTYEX('InnovatorSolutions', 'Collation') AS database_collation;
```

## Fix

**Short term:** make temp tables follow the database collation:

```sql
CREATE TABLE #part_ids (
    id CHAR(32) COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT PRIMARY KEY
);
```

**Long term:** install the instance with the same collation as the source server, and add it to the environment checklist. Rebuilding the system databases on an existing instance is possible but disruptive.

## Notes

Ask for the source server collation **before** the customer's DBA installs the new instance. It's a two-minute question that saves a day.
entries.author: Priya Raman

entries.title: Teamcenter file downloads fail because the FSC advertises an unreachable host name
entries.summary: Rich Client users outside the server VLAN could log in but not open datasets. The FSC in fmsmaster was configured with a short internal host name that client machines could not resolve.
entries.content:
## Symptom

- Login and structure navigation work.
- Opening or downloading any dataset hangs, then fails with an FMS read error.
- It only affects users on the office network. Users working on the server itself are fine.

## Root cause

In the FMS master configuration, the FSC was registered with the short name the installer picked up:

```xml
<fsc id="FSC_tcapp01" address="http://tcapp01:4544" ismaster="true">
```

Clients get this address from the server and then connect **directly** to the FSC. `tcapp01` doesn't resolve on the office network, and port 4544 was only open inside the server VLAN.

## Fix

1. Use a fully qualified name (or a DNS alias) that every client can resolve:

   ```xml
   <fsc id="FSC_tcapp01" address="http://tcapp01.corp.example.com:4544" ismaster="true">
   ```

2. Open TCP 4544 from the client networks to the FSC host.
3. Restart the FSC service and check it from a client machine:

   ```bat
   fscadmin -s http://tcapp01.corp.example.com:4544 ./status
   ```

4. On affected clients, stop the FCC so it reloads its configuration: `fccstat -kill`.

## Notes

Test FMS from a real client machine during installation, not from the server. Checks run on the server hide this whole class of problem.
entries.author: Lukas Becker

entries.title: Large STEP uploads rejected with HTTP 404.13 by an IIS-hosted integration endpoint
entries.summary: Uploading CAD files over about 28 MB to a custom ASP.NET endpoint returned 404.13. IIS request filtering limits the request body to 30,000,000 bytes by default.
entries.content:
## Symptom

Small files upload fine. Anything larger than about 28 MB fails before our code runs:

```text
HTTP Error 404.13 - Not Found
The request filtering module is configured to deny a request that exceeds the request content length.
```

It's confusing because it looks like a *not found* error.

## Root cause

Two separate limits apply:

| Layer | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IIS request filtering | `maxAllowedContentLength` (bytes) | 30,000,000 (~28.6 MB) |
| ASP.NET | `maxRequestLength` (KB) | 4,096 (4 MB) |

IIS rejects the request first, which is why the error comes from IIS and not from ASP.NET.

## Fix

Raise **both** limits in the endpoint's `web.config`, and keep them consistent:

```xml
<configuration>
  <system.web>
    <!-- KB: 1 GB -->
    <httpRuntime maxRequestLength="1048576" executionTimeout="3600" />
  </system.web>
  <system.webServer>
    <security>
      <requestFiltering>
        <!-- bytes: 1 GB -->
        <requestLimits maxAllowedContentLength="1073741824" />
      </requestFiltering>
    </security>
  </system.webServer>
</configuration>
```

## Notes

- Set limits based on the largest realistic file, not the maximum possible value.
- A load balancer or WAF in front of IIS often has its own body-size limit. Check it too.

entries.title: Slow Aras searches after bulk data migration: rebuild statistics and indexes
entries.summary: After loading 1.2 million legacy Parts, search grids took 20+ seconds. Outdated statistics and heavily fragmented indexes were the cause; a full statistics update fixed it immediately.
entries.content:
## Symptom

Directly after the data migration go-live, simple Part searches took 20–40 seconds. The same searches on the test system, which had the same data, took under a second.

## Root cause

The migration loaded millions of rows in a few hours. Automatic statistics updates only sample the data and hadn't caught up, so SQL Server picked plans designed for a nearly empty table. The bulk inserts also left the indexes badly fragmented.

## Fix

```sql
-- 1. Refresh statistics on the big tables with a full scan
UPDATE STATISTICS innovator.PART WITH FULLSCAN;
UPDATE STATISTICS innovator.PART_BOM WITH FULLSCAN;

-- 2. Check fragmentation
SELECT OBJECT_NAME(ips.object_id) AS table_name, i.name AS index_name,
       ips.avg_fragmentation_in_percent, ips.page_count
FROM sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats(DB_ID(), NULL, NULL, NULL, 'LIMITED') ips
JOIN sys.indexes i ON i.object_id = ips.object_id AND i.index_id = ips.index_id
WHERE ips.page_count > 1000 AND ips.avg_fragmentation_in_percent > 30
ORDER BY ips.avg_fragmentation_in_percent DESC;

-- 3. Rebuild the worst offenders
ALTER INDEX ALL ON innovator.PART REBUILD;
```

## Notes

- Make "update statistics with full scan" the **last step of every migration runbook**.
- Make sure a regular index and statistics maintenance job exists. Many customer databases have none.
entries.author: Daniel Okafor

entries.title: Plan for the compatibility level change when moving to SQL Server 2022
entries.summary: Restoring an older database on SQL Server 2022 keeps its old compatibility level. Raise it to 160 on purpose, with Query Store enabled, so plan regressions can be spotted and fixed.
entries.content:
## Background

A database restored on a newer SQL Server keeps its compatibility level, e.g. **130** from SQL Server 2016. It runs, but without the newer optimizer. If the level is raised without a plan, a few queries can suddenly get much slower because of the new cardinality estimator.

## Recommended approach

1. Restore and keep the **old level** for the first functional tests.
2. Turn on Query Store so there's a baseline:

   ```sql
   ALTER DATABASE InnovatorSolutions SET QUERY_STORE = ON;
   ALTER DATABASE InnovatorSolutions SET QUERY_STORE (OPERATION_MODE = READ_WRITE);
   ```

3. Run the regression test set and typical user workload.
4. Raise the level:

   ```sql
   ALTER DATABASE InnovatorSolutions SET COMPATIBILITY_LEVEL = 160;
   ```

5. Run the same workload again and compare in *Query Store → Regressed Queries*. Force the old plan for any query that got worse.

## Fallback

If many queries regress and there's no time to tune them, keep level 160 but use the legacy estimator for this database:

```sql
ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET LEGACY_CARDINALITY_ESTIMATION = ON;
```

Write this down as technical debt. Don't leave it undocumented.
entries.author: Priya Raman

entries.title: Clearing stale Teamcenter object locks after a tcserver crash
entries.summary: After a server VM crashed, users got "object is locked" errors on items nobody had open. The clearlocks utility releases locks held by dead processes, but only run it when those processes are really gone.
entries.content:
## Symptom

After an unplanned restart of an application server VM, several users couldn't check out or modify items. They got lock errors on objects nobody was editing.

## Root cause

The `tcserver` processes that held the locks died with the VM, so they never released them. Teamcenter still treats those processes' locks as valid.

## Fix

1. Confirm the processes are really gone (Server Manager admin page, Task Manager on the host).
2. From a Teamcenter command prompt with the environment set (`tc_profilevars`):

   ```bat
   clearlocks -u=infodba -p=******** -g=dba -assert_all_dead
   ```

3. Ask users to retry. The locks are released straight away.

## Warning

`-assert_all_dead` tells Teamcenter that **no** tcserver processes on the recorded nodes are alive. If any live server still holds a lock, you can corrupt data. On a busy multi-server system, target only the crashed node, or do it in a maintenance window.

## Notes

Add this to the customer's outage runbook with the exact command, so on-call staff don't have to search for it at 2 a.m.
entries.author: Lukas Becker

entries.title: Getting an OAuth token for the Aras REST API from an integration script
entries.summary: Integrations calling the Aras OData REST API need a bearer token from the Aras OAuth server. Discover the token endpoint first, then use the password grant with an MD5-hashed password.
entries.content:
## Steps

1. **Discover the OAuth server** that belongs to the Innovator instance.
2. **Read its OpenID configuration** to find the token endpoint.
3. **Request a token** and send it as a bearer token to `/Server/odata`.

```powershell
$innovator = "https://plm.example.com/InnovatorServer"
$database  = "InnovatorSolutions"
$user      = "svc_erp_sync"
$password  = $env:ARAS_SVC_PASSWORD

# 1 + 2: discovery
$discovery = Invoke-RestMethod "$innovator/Server/OAuthServerDiscovery.aspx"
$authority = $discovery.locations[0].uri
$oidc      = Invoke-RestMethod "$($authority.TrimEnd('/'))/.well-known/openid-configuration"

# Aras expects the MD5 hash of the password
$md5  = [System.Security.Cryptography.MD5]::Create()
$hash = -join ($md5.ComputeHash([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($password)) | ForEach-Object { $_.ToString("x2") })

# 3: token (password grant)
$token = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri $oidc.token_endpoint -Body @{
  grant_type = "password"
  scope      = "Innovator"
  client_id  = "IOMApp"
  username   = $user
  password   = $hash
  database   = $database
}

$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $($token.access_token)" }
Invoke-RestMethod "$innovator/server/odata/Part?`$top=5&`$select=item_number,name" -Headers $headers
```

## Notes

- Tokens expire (check `expires_in`). Long-running jobs should get a new token instead of assuming one lasts all night.
- Use a dedicated service account with only the permissions the integration needs.
- Never commit the password. Read it from a secret store or environment variable.
entries.author: Daniel Okafor

entries.title: Making PLM-to-ERP BOM transfers safe to retry
entries.summary: A network glitch during a BOM transfer created duplicate lines in ERP when the job was retried. Design every message to be idempotent, with a stable message key and upsert semantics on the receiving side.
entries.content:
## What went wrong

The integration sent a released BOM to ERP. The ERP side processed it, but the acknowledgement was lost in a timeout. The middleware retried, and ERP added the BOM lines **a second time**.

## Principles we now apply

1. **Stable message key.** Build it from business identity, not from a random ID created on each send:

   ```text
   <item_number>|<revision>|<release_timestamp>
   ```

2. **Receiver upserts, never blindly inserts.** If the key has been processed already, return the earlier result.
3. **Send whole state, not deltas,** where possible. "This is the complete BOM for rev C" is safe to apply twice; "add line 40" is not.
4. **Retries with backoff and a dead-letter queue.** After N failures, park the message and alert a human rather than retrying forever.
5. **Trace every message.** Log the key on both sides so support can answer "did ERP get rev C?" in one query.

## Checklist for new integrations

- [ ] Message key defined and documented
- [ ] Receiver handles duplicates
- [ ] Retry policy and dead-letter handling agreed
- [ ] Monitoring and alerting owner named
entries.environment: Aras Innovator → SAP S/4HANA via middleware
entries.author: Sofia Martins

entries.title: Aras package import fails because packages are imported in the wrong order
entries.summary: A configuration deployment to production failed halfway because one package referenced ItemTypes defined in another. Keep an explicit, dependency-ordered import manifest and test the full deployment on a fresh copy.
entries.content:
## Symptom

The deployment worked in test but failed in production. The import log showed items that couldn't be added because a referenced ItemType, List or Property didn't exist yet.

## Root cause

In test, the packages had been imported **one at a time over several weeks**, so dependencies were always there already. In production, everything was imported in one run, in the wrong order, from a manifest that was built by hand.

## Fix

- Keep one manifest file under version control and list the packages **in dependency order**: lists and ItemTypes first, then relationships, forms, Methods and finally workflows and permissions.
- Declare package dependencies explicitly so the import tool can check them.
- Before every production deployment, do a **dress rehearsal** on a fresh restore of production, using exactly the files and manifest that will be used.

## Notes

- Record the import log for every environment and keep it with the release notes.
- A failed import can leave a half-applied configuration. Make sure there's a tested database backup right before the run.
entries.environment: Aras Innovator 12.0 SP18, Package Import Export Utility
entries.author: Tom de Vries

entries.title: Run PLM requirements workshops data-model first
entries.summary: Workshops that started from screens and forms kept going in circles. Starting from the data model (what the objects are, how they relate, and who owns them) gave shorter workshops and fewer late changes.
entries.content:
## Lesson learned

In an early project, workshops were organised by screen ("what should the Part form look like?"). Every session reopened decisions from the last one, because nobody had agreed on what a Part, a Document or a Change actually *is* for this customer.

## What works better

1. **Object inventory first.** List the business objects in the customer's own words. Map each one to a standard type or flag it as custom.
2. **Relationships and cardinality.** Draw them on a whiteboard: *Can a Document belong to several Parts? Is a CAD model a Document?*
3. **Lifecycle per object.** States, who moves an object between states, and what is locked in each state.
4. **Ownership and permissions.** Who creates, who approves, who can only read.
5. **Only then** forms, grids and reports.

## Practical tips

- Use the customer's real data. Bring three real Parts and a real change request to the first workshop.
- Write decisions down **during** the session and read them back at the end.
- Timebox open questions: give each an owner and a due date, and don't let them block the rest.
entries.author: Priya Raman

entries.title: Definition of Done for Aras configuration changes
entries.summary: A shared checklist the team agreed on for when a configuration change counts as done. It cut down on "works on my database" problems during deployments.
entries.content:
A change is **done** when all of these are true:

- [ ] Change is in a named **package** (not loose in the database) and exported to version control
- [ ] Package dependencies declared and the manifest updated
- [ ] Imported successfully on a **clean** copy of the target environment
- [ ] Server Methods compile, with no warnings ignored without a comment
- [ ] Permissions checked with a **non-admin** test user
- [ ] Regression scenario for the affected process executed and recorded
- [ ] Customer-facing behaviour change written in the release notes
- [ ] Reviewer (someone other than the author) has looked at AML and Method code

## Why "non-admin" is on the list

Most "works in test, fails in production" issues we saw came from testing as an administrator. An admin skips permission checks and hides missing grants.

## How we use it

The checklist is pasted into every change ticket. A reviewer only approves once every box is ticked or has a written reason.
entries.author: Maya Jansen

entries.title: HTTP Error 500.19 (0x8007000d) after moving a site to a new IIS server
entries.summary: The copied site failed immediately with 500.19 and error code 0x8007000d. web.config referenced modules that weren't installed on the new server, such as URL Rewrite or the ASP.NET Core Hosting Bundle.
entries.content:
## Symptom

After copying the web application to a freshly built server, every request returned:

```text
HTTP Error 500.19 - Internal Server Error
The requested page cannot be accessed because the related configuration data for the page is invalid.
Error Code 0x8007000d
```

## Root cause

`0x8007000d` means IIS found configuration it doesn't understand. Usually it isn't a typo. `web.config` contains a section for a module that isn't installed:

| Section in web.config | Missing component |
| --- | --- |
| `<rewrite>` | IIS URL Rewrite Module |
| `<aspNetCore>` | ASP.NET Core Hosting Bundle (ANCM) |

## Fix

1. Search `web.config` for `<rewrite>` and `<aspNetCore>`.
2. Install the missing component(s). For .NET-based products, install the **Hosting Bundle** version that matches the runtime the application needs.
3. Restart IIS so the module is registered:

   ```bat
   iisreset
   ```

## Notes

Keep a server prerequisites checklist per product version and install everything on it **before** copying the application.
entries.author: Daniel Okafor

entries.title: RDP over customer VPN freezes every few minutes: lower the MTU
entries.summary: Remote desktop sessions through a customer's VPN kept freezing while small tasks like ping worked. Packets were too large for the tunnel; lowering the MTU on the VPN adapter fixed it.
entries.content:
## Symptom

- VPN connects fine, and ping and small web pages work.
- RDP to the customer's servers freezes for 10–30 seconds at a time, especially when screens redraw.
- File copies over SMB stall.

## Root cause

The VPN adds overhead to every packet, so full-size packets (1500 bytes) no longer fit. When the network blocks the ICMP messages that would normally tell the sender to use smaller packets, large packets silently disappear.

## Find the largest packet that fits

```bat
REM -f = don't fragment, -l = payload size. Lower until it succeeds.
ping -f -l 1400 customer-server.corp.local
ping -f -l 1372 customer-server.corp.local
```

MTU = largest working payload + 28 bytes (IP and ICMP headers).

## Fix

Set the MTU on the VPN adapter (run as administrator):

```bat
netsh interface ipv4 show subinterfaces
netsh interface ipv4 set subinterface "Customer VPN" mtu=1400 store=persistent
```

## Notes

Share the working value with colleagues on the same customer. It's usually the same for everyone on that VPN.

entries.title: Moving an Aras file vault to a new server without breaking file links
entries.summary: How we moved 2 TB of vault files to new storage over a weekend. Pre-copy with robocopy, do a short final sync during downtime, then update the vault URL.
entries.content:
## Approach

Copying 2 TB takes too long for a normal downtime window, so we split it into a **pre-copy** and a **final delta sync**.

### 1. Pre-copy (days before, system online)

```bat
robocopy D:\Vault \\newvault01\D$\Vault /MIR /COPY:DAT /DCOPY:DAT /R:2 /W:5 /MT:16 /NP /LOG:C:\temp\vault-precopy.log
```

Run it again each night. Each run only copies what changed.

### 2. Cut-over (downtime)

1. Stop users from writing: put Innovator in maintenance mode or stop the Vault app pool.
2. Run the same robocopy command once more. This final delta usually takes minutes.
3. On the new server, set up the Vault web application with the same configuration.
4. In Innovator, update the **Vault** item's URL to the new server.
5. Test: download an old file, upload a new one and check it arrives on the new storage.

## Pitfalls

- `/MIR` **deletes** files in the destination that don't exist in the source. Double-check the direction before you press Enter.
- Keep the old vault read-only for a few weeks as a fallback. Don't delete it on the weekend of the move.
- Compare file counts and total size from the robocopy summary with the source before you go live.
entries.author: Sofia Martins
